title: Probabilistic batch allocator and quantization safeguard for mixed workloads
author: Priya Shah
description: Context: Customer workloads show a mix of small low-latency requests and bursty background inference. Static defaults for batch sizes and quantization profiles either waste GPU cycles or cause tail-latency spikes. This PR adds a probabilistic batch allocator (PBA) that selects batch sizes at request-aggregation time using a lightweight cost/latency sampler, plus a runtime quantization safeguard that prevents aggressive qprofiles from applying when predicted output-risk is high. Motivation: reduce unit-cost (tokens/second GPU) while preserving 99th-percentile latency SLOs and avoiding silent quality regressions. Design: - PBA observes short-window stats (arrival rate, sequence-length histogram, KV-cache hit ratio) and samples a small set of candidate batch sizes. Each candidate is scored by an internal utility function combining expected throughput and p99 latency risk; the allocator picks the batch size probabilistically proportional to utility to preserve diversity and avoid pathological swing behaviors. - Quantization safeguard evaluates a cheap signal derived from the model's early-token logits (calibrated per-model) and recent eval-set deltas; if the risk score exceeds threshold, the runtime falls back to the next-safer qprofile or routes to a non-quantized fallback. - Integration points: serving/runtime/batcher (new pba module), runtime/quant (safeguard hook), console -> optimize suggestions (UI hints), and canary rollout config. Checklist: - [x] Core allocator implementation + docs for scoring function and safety knobs. - [x] Quant risk estimator + per-model calibration job. - [x] Unit tests for allocator and quant guard heuristics. - [x] End-to-end replay tests against mix-traffic traces (T4/A100). - [x] Canary rollout script and dashboard panels. Testing details: Offline replay across 10 representative traces showed median unit-cost reduction of 14% and p99 latency change within +/-2ms for web-equivalent traces. For very bursty RL-like traces we saw 22% unit-cost wins with careful qprofile fallbacks. Safety: quant safeguard prevented three regressions during replay that would have increased token-level perplexity by >1.5x. Backwards compatibility: allocator is opt-in via route config; quant safeguards default to enabled but can be tuned by model owners. Rollout plan: 1) internal alpha on dedicated clusters (A100) 2) 1% canary on hosted region us-west-2 3) staged ramp with automated rollback if p99 increases >5% or eval-set regressions detected. Related: ENG-8702 (econ primitives), ENG-9021 (quant risk infra).

review_thread: Ethan Cole (reviewer): Nice design. Two questions: (1) How do you prevent correlated swings where many requests pick large batches and cause latency spikes? (2) Please justify the probabilistic selection vs. a deterministic cost-optimized pick.

Author (Priya Shah): For (1) the sampler includes an anti-correlation term (recent-picked-size decay) so repeated picks bias away from the same size; we added a short circuit to cap aggregate batch size under load. For (2) probabilistic selection intentionally maintains diversity to avoid local minima and improves stability for multimodal traffic; deterministic picks had higher observed p99 variance in replay tests—added numbers to docs/rdoc/pba_design.md.
Marta Ruiz (reviewer): Implementation looks good. Please add metrics for 'chosen_batch_distribution' and expose a debug endpoint to query current scoring weights per route.
Author (Priya Shah): Added chosen_batch_distribution histogram (serving/metrics) and a /debug/pba/stats endpoint restricted to internal tokens. Updated tests to validate metric emission.

Ibrahim Khan (SRE): We need a safe default that won't change behavior for existing routes. Confirmed allocator is opt-in; also request that canary workflow includes automated rollback on increased error-rate.

Author (Priya Shah): Confirmed opt-in default. Canary workflow now contains rollback conditions: p99 increase > 5% or error-rate spike > 2x baseline; health check uses both production traces and eval-set checkouts.

release_notes: Add probabilistic batch allocator (opt-in per-route) to improve GPU utilization for mixed workloads.
Introduce quantization safeguard to automatically fall back to safer qprofiles when output-risk is detected.
Expose pba metrics (chosen_batch_distribution) and debug endpoint for internal use.
Canary rollout automation with automated rollback on p99 or error spikes.
